Landlords must also register units annually, give required tenant notices, and file eviction notices with LAHD. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 165.00 et seq..

A landlord who demolishes a Protected Unit for new construction must pay relocation assistance at the higher of state Housing Crisis Act or City amounts, with lower income tenants receiving enhanced standardized payments ($115,480 extremely low, $96,750 very low, $87,450 low income for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027), and must provide other occupant protections. Above-low-income tenants receive the RSO/JCO amounts. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Ordinances No. 188481 and No. 188482.

Before any no-fault eviction from a unit covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and pay relocation assistance based on the tenant's status (eligible or qualified), length of tenancy and income. For July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, amounts are $11,000 or $14,400 for eligible households and $23,150 or $27,400 for qualified households, with reduced amounts for Mom and Pop owner-occupancy evictions ($10,550 / $21,250) and one month's rent for JCO single-family homes owned by natural persons. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: LAMC 151.09, 151.30, 165.03, 165.06.

For RSO units, rent may be increased only once every 12 months, by the allowable rent increase percentage set by LAHD. As of February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer add an extra percentage for utilities, and rent can reset to market rate only after certain vacancies or evictions. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Chapter XV, Article 1.

The RSO covers interest payments on security deposits for RSO units. This page does not state the rate or timing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Chapter XV, Article 1.

A0341.explanation: No one may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust or conspiracy to restrain trade. No one may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. A common pricing algorithm is any method, including software, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

Landlords may charge a capped screening fee only to cover the cost of screening, such as a credit report. They must give receipts, itemized costs, a copy of any credit report and a refund of unused fees, and they must accept a reusable screening report. They cannot charge a fee when no unit is available, and they must return fees to applicants not selected unless they use a first-qualified-applicant policy. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on year built, owner occupied, owner is corporation, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26 – 2/28/27 the amount is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower income households (80% AMI or lower) displaced by demolition of their units for new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code § 7260 et seq. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6.
Coverage depends on year built, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Housing providers may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests not leading to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot have blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and time elapsed. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

Housing providers may not refuse to rent to, or set different terms for, applicants or tenants because of how they will pay rent, including Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. They must also comply with the requirements of rental assistance programs, such as completing required paperwork. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

When an applicant has a government rent subsidy, a housing provider may not use the applicant's credit history unless it offers the option to give other lawful, verifiable proof of ability to pay the tenant's share of rent. If the applicant chooses this option, the provider must give reasonable time to respond and must reasonably consider that evidence instead of credit history. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. A small landlord (a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units) may charge up to two months' rent, except to a service member. The landlord must return the remaining deposit with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant moves out. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

The proposed ordinance would make it unlawful to sell, license, or provide an algorithmic device to a landlord. It would also bar a landlord from using one to set rental rates or occupancy levels, where the device uses nonpublic competitor data to advise or recommend rents or occupancy. This document is a draft with a blank final passage date, so it does not show the ordinance was adopted. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.D. Mun. Code §§ 98.1101-98.1104.
Coverage depends on year built, owner occupied, owner is corporation, which the public records do not include. Source: San Diego Mun. Code §§ 98.0701–98.0710.

Landlords may not refuse, renew, end or restrict a tenancy, misrepresent availability, or advertise in a discriminatory way based on a person's source of income, including rental assistance and housing vouchers. Income standards must count all of a tenant's sources of income and the combined income of co-tenants and cosigners. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: San Diego Mun. Code §§ 98.0801–98.0806.

A0342.explanation: Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Cambridge City Council policy order.

Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not discriminate in viewing or renting an apartment or in the terms and conditions of a tenancy based on protected categories, including source of income (Section 8 and public benefits). They may use any reasonable selection standard, such as ability to pay rent, only if it is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 14.04.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222, 194th General Court.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. S.2983, 194th General Court.

Only a licensed broker or salesperson may charge prospective tenants a fee for finding housing. The broker must give the applicant written notice at the first personal meeting stating the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, and have the applicant sign it or record a refusal. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.00.

A broker fee for finding a rental home may only be paid by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally hired and contracted with the licensed broker or salesperson. A landlord cannot pass the fee for a broker it hired on to the tenant. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a lock and key. As amended by St. 2025, c. 9, effective August 1, 2025, the limit expressly covers payments to the landlord's agent (e.g., broker fees); before that date the text applied to 'lessor' only. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B.

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often, notice equal to the rent interval or 30 days, whichever is longer. This section does not require the landlord to give a reason. For nonpayment of rent, a 14-day written notice to quit is enough, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12.

Anyone renting housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a federal, state or local housing subsidy, such as rental assistance or a voucher. They also may not discriminate because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4.

A landlord may not charge a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be kept in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (less lawful, itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B.

A0343.explanation: Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Newark, N.J., Code § 19:2-3.1; § 19:2-3.2.

Defines an unconscionable rent as a residential rent increase that is exceedingly harsh or unreasonable, exceeds the increase in the landlord's expenses, and is not comparable to rents at similar properties. For properties under a redevelopment or financial agreement, rent above the approved pro-forma is per se unconscionable. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Newark, N.J., Code § 2:10-11.1.
Coverage depends on units, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Newark Rev. Gen. Ord. ch. 2:31, Art. 1, §§ 2:31-1 to 2:31-9.

A0344.explanation: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ban is enforced both by public authorities and through private lawsuits. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Code § 218-12.

Jersey City regulates rent increases under its Rent Control Ordinance, which the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers and enforces. Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt, and other exemptions in the ordinance may be requested. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Mun. Code ch. 260.

A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. The cap is adjusted each January 1 for CPI increases, starting the year after enactment. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the good causes listed in the statute, which the landlord must prove in court. A Notice to Quit (and in some cases a Notice to Cease) is required for every ground except nonpayment of rent. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

New Jersey has no statewide numeric rent cap, but a landlord may only evict for nonpayment of a rent increase if the increase is not unconscionable and complies with any municipal rent ordinance; the increase requires termination of the old lease with a Notice to Quit and notice of rent increase, and rent cannot be raised mid-lease. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone with a Section 8 HUD voucher based solely on that source of income. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq..

Housing providers may not ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record, orally or in writing, until after making a conditional offer. After that, they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, and may withdraw the offer only after an individualized assessment showing a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest. The act takes effect on the first day of the seventh month after the June 18, 2021 enactment, which works out to 2022-01-01. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64 (P.L. 2021, c.110).

A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any yearly increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid rent, including last month's rent, counts toward the cap; the deposit must be held in an interest-bearing account in trust for the tenant and returned with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2; N.J.S.A. 46:8-19; N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1; N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

New Jersey's security deposit law applies to all rental units used as homes. The only exception is owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units, and that exception ends once the tenant gives the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-2.

Landlords who raise a current tenant's rent by more than 10% year over year at lease renewal must give written disclosures before the increase takes effect: an itemization of costs behind the increase, whether a rent algorithm was used, notice of the tenant's right to sue if the increase is unconscionable or unlawful, and Division of Housing contact information. This is a disclosure rule, not a cap on the amount of the increase. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-1.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Hoboken City Code ch. 155, §§ 155-3, 155-4, 155-5.

A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. The cap is adjusted each January 1 for CPI increases, starting the year after enactment. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the good causes listed in the statute, which the landlord must prove in court. A Notice to Quit (and in some cases a Notice to Cease) is required for every ground except nonpayment of rent. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

New Jersey has no statewide numeric rent cap, but a landlord may only evict for nonpayment of a rent increase if the increase is not unconscionable and complies with any municipal rent ordinance; the increase requires termination of the old lease with a Notice to Quit and notice of rent increase, and rent cannot be raised mid-lease. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone with a Section 8 HUD voucher based solely on that source of income. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq..

Housing providers may not ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record, orally or in writing, until after making a conditional offer. After that, they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, and may withdraw the offer only after an individualized assessment showing a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest. The act takes effect on the first day of the seventh month after the June 18, 2021 enactment, which works out to 2022-01-01. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64 (P.L. 2021, c.110).

A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any yearly increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid rent, including last month's rent, counts toward the cap; the deposit must be held in an interest-bearing account in trust for the tenant and returned with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2; N.J.S.A. 46:8-19; N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1; N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

New Jersey's security deposit law applies to all rental units used as homes. The only exception is owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units, and that exception ends once the tenant gives the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A0349.explanation: No one may sell, license or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Landlords may not use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels. A coordinated pricing algorithm is one that uses nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63, as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S..

An owner who charges a fee for a credit report or to process a rental application must first give the applicant a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the state maximum fee cap. This can be in the application or in a separate disclosure given before the fee is received. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.010.

Owners and their agents cannot charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees tied to a roommate leaving or to adding or replacing a roommate. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.016.

Owners must pay relocation assistance to tenants evicted for owner move-in. The payment is adjusted each year for inflation, and the Rent Board publishes the new amounts. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for rent debt below one month's HUD Fair Market Rent, bars eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease, tightens lease-breach evictions, and requires eviction notices to reference the Rent Board and be filed with it within three business days. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

Owners who evict tenants to remove a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions, adjusted yearly for inflation. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.77.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions. This includes refusing to rent, ending a tenancy, charging a higher deposit or rent, or refusing to add a family member because of criminal history. If a landlord takes action based on criminal history under an exception, the landlord must give written notice and a chance to respond. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.106.

Landlords of units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year. If the tenant moves out before the end of the year, the landlord must pay a prorated amount. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

No one may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust or conspiracy to restrain trade. No one may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. A common pricing algorithm is any method, including software, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

Landlords may charge a capped screening fee only to cover the cost of screening, such as a credit report. They must give receipts, itemized costs, a copy of any credit report and a refund of unused fees, and they must accept a reusable screening report. They cannot charge a fee when no unit is available, and they must return fees to applicants not selected unless they use a first-qualified-applicant policy. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on year built, owner occupied, owner is corporation, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26 – 2/28/27 the amount is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower income households (80% AMI or lower) displaced by demolition of their units for new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code § 7260 et seq. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6.
Coverage depends on year built, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Housing providers may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests not leading to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot have blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and time elapsed. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

Housing providers may not refuse to rent to, or set different terms for, applicants or tenants because of how they will pay rent, including Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. They must also comply with the requirements of rental assistance programs, such as completing required paperwork. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

When an applicant has a government rent subsidy, a housing provider may not use the applicant's credit history unless it offers the option to give other lawful, verifiable proof of ability to pay the tenant's share of rent. If the applicant chooses this option, the provider must give reasonable time to respond and must reasonably consider that evidence instead of credit history. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. A small landlord (a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units) may charge up to two months' rent, except to a service member. The landlord must return the remaining deposit with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant moves out. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

A0350.explanation: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ban is enforced both by public authorities and through private lawsuits. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Code § 218-12.

Jersey City regulates rent increases under its Rent Control Ordinance, which the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers and enforces. Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt, and other exemptions in the ordinance may be requested. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Mun. Code ch. 260.

Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq..

Prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices, such as software that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for vacant units, to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The end of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause, and removing housing services such as parking, storage or laundry also requires just cause. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9.

A landlord who evicts tenants under the Ellis Act (withdrawing units from the rental market) must pay relocation money to each tenant, up to a per-unit maximum. There is an extra amount for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Amounts adjust each year based on the date the eviction notice is served. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A.

A landlord who evicts for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation money to each tenant, up to a per-unit maximum. There is an extra amount for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Amounts adjust each year based on the date the eviction notice is served. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units in San Francisco, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period (March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026) allowed 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37.

Landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the rate the Rent Board publishes each year. The rate is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code Ch. 49.

A0352.explanation: When a lease expires or a periodic tenancy ends, a landlord may not ask for or collect a rent increase larger than the CPI change from 15 months to 3 months before the proposed increase, and never more than 4%. The limit applies once per 12 months regardless of tenant turnover, ownership change or vacancy. No increase is allowed if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance with codes or is not registered. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Newark, N.J., Code § 19:2-3.1; § 19:2-3.2.

Defines an unconscionable rent as a residential rent increase that is exceedingly harsh or unreasonable, exceeds the increase in the landlord's expenses, and is not comparable to rents at similar properties. For properties under a redevelopment or financial agreement, rent above the approved pro-forma is per se unconscionable. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Newark, N.J., Code § 2:10-11.1.

Landlords must also register units annually, give required tenant notices, and file eviction notices with LAHD. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 165.00 et seq..

A landlord who demolishes a Protected Unit for new construction must pay relocation assistance at the higher of state Housing Crisis Act or City amounts, with lower income tenants receiving enhanced standardized payments ($115,480 extremely low, $96,750 very low, $87,450 low income for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027), and must provide other occupant protections. Above-low-income tenants receive the RSO/JCO amounts. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Ordinances No. 188481 and No. 188482.

A0354.explanation: A landlord or foreclosing owner who plans to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy, including by not renewing a lease, must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or non-renewal notice. The landlord must also send a copy of the notice to quit or non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. This is a notice requirement only; it does not limit the reasons a landlord may end a tenancy. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Ordinance Sec. 10-11.7.

In Boston, landlords may not discriminate in renting housing based on protected characteristics, including the use of rental assistance such as Section 8, social security disability, and veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is housing discrimination. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Fair Housing Regulations.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222, 194th General Court.

Only a licensed broker or salesperson may charge prospective tenants a fee for finding housing. The broker must give the applicant written notice at the first personal meeting stating the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, and have the applicant sign it or record a refusal. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.00.

A broker fee for finding a rental home may only be paid by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally hired and contracted with the licensed broker or salesperson. A landlord cannot pass the fee for a broker it hired on to the tenant. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a lock and key. As amended by St. 2025, c. 9, effective August 1, 2025, the limit expressly covers payments to the landlord's agent (e.g., broker fees); before that date the text applied to 'lessor' only. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B.

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often, notice equal to the rent interval or 30 days, whichever is longer. This section does not require the landlord to give a reason. For nonpayment of rent, a 14-day written notice to quit is enough, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12.

Anyone renting housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a federal, state or local housing subsidy, such as rental assistance or a voucher. They also may not discriminate because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4.

Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B.

Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

Landlords may charge a capped screening fee only to cover the cost of screening, such as a credit report. They must give receipts, itemized costs, a copy of any credit report and a refund of unused fees, and they must accept a reusable screening report. They cannot charge a fee when no unit is available, and they must return fees to applicants not selected unless they use a first-qualified-applicant policy. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
A stricter local rule governs this building instead. The Los Angeles rule on this topic covers this building. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26 – 2/28/27 the amount is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower income households (80% AMI or lower) displaced by demolition of their units for new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code § 7260 et seq. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6.

Over any 12-month period, an owner may not raise the gross rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months. If the same tenant stays, the rent may be raised in no more than two increments in that period. Owners may set any rent for a new tenancy once all prior tenants have left. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Housing providers may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests not leading to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot have blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and time elapsed. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

Housing providers may not refuse to rent to, or set different terms for, applicants or tenants because of how they will pay rent, including Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. They must also comply with the requirements of rental assistance programs, such as completing required paperwork. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

When an applicant has a government rent subsidy, a housing provider may not use the applicant's credit history unless it offers the option to give other lawful, verifiable proof of ability to pay the tenant's share of rent. If the applicant chooses this option, the provider must give reasonable time to respond and must reasonably consider that evidence instead of credit history. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. A small landlord (a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units) may charge up to two months' rent, except to a service member. The landlord must return the remaining deposit with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant moves out. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Los Angeles City Council File No. 24-1031.

Landlords of covered rental units in Los Angeles may not end a tenancy without one of the listed at-fault or no-fault just causes, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. Landlords must also register units annually, give required tenant notices, and file eviction notices with LAHD. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 165.00 et seq..

A landlord who demolishes a Protected Unit for new construction must pay relocation assistance at the higher of state Housing Crisis Act or City amounts, with lower income tenants receiving enhanced standardized payments ($115,480 extremely low, $96,750 very low, $87,450 low income for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027), and must provide other occupant protections. Above-low-income tenants receive the RSO/JCO amounts. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Ordinances No. 188481 and No. 188482.

A0356.explanation: A landlord or foreclosing owner who plans to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy, including by not renewing a lease, must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or non-renewal notice. The landlord must also send a copy of the notice to quit or non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. This is a notice requirement only; it does not limit the reasons a landlord may end a tenancy. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Ordinance Sec. 10-11.7.

In Boston, landlords may not discriminate in renting housing based on protected characteristics, including the use of rental assistance such as Section 8, social security disability, and veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is housing discrimination. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Fair Housing Regulations.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222, 194th General Court.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. S.2983, 194th General Court.

Only a licensed broker or salesperson may charge prospective tenants a fee for finding housing. The broker must give the applicant written notice at the first personal meeting stating the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, and have the applicant sign it or record a refusal. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.00.

A broker fee for finding a rental home may only be paid by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally hired and contracted with the licensed broker or salesperson. A landlord cannot pass the fee for a broker it hired on to the tenant. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a lock and key. As amended by St. 2025, c. 9, effective August 1, 2025, the limit expressly covers payments to the landlord's agent (e.g., broker fees); before that date the text applied to 'lessor' only. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B.

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often, notice equal to the rent interval or 30 days, whichever is longer. This section does not require the landlord to give a reason. For nonpayment of rent, a 14-day written notice to quit is enough, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12.

Anyone renting housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a federal, state or local housing subsidy, such as rental assistance or a voucher. They also may not discriminate because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4.

A landlord may not charge a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be kept in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (less lawful, itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B.

A0357.explanation: No one may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust or conspiracy to restrain trade. No one may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. A common pricing algorithm is any method, including software, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.

Civ. Code § 1950.5.

Prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices, such as software that analyzes nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents for vacant units, to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.10C.

A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The end of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause, and removing housing services such as parking, storage or laundry also requires just cause. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9.

A landlord who evicts tenants under the Ellis Act (withdrawing units from the rental market) must pay relocation money to each tenant, up to a per-unit maximum. There is an extra amount for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Amounts adjust each year based on the date the eviction notice is served. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9A.

A landlord who evicts for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation money to each tenant, up to a per-unit maximum. There is an extra amount for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Amounts adjust each year based on the date the eviction notice is served. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

Landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the rate the Rent Board publishes each year. The rate is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code Ch. 49.

A0358.explanation: Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Newark, N.J., Code § 19:2-3.1; § 19:2-3.2.

Defines an unconscionable rent as a residential rent increase that is exceedingly harsh or unreasonable, exceeds the increase in the landlord's expenses, and is not comparable to rents at similar properties. For properties under a redevelopment or financial agreement, rent above the approved pro-forma is per se unconscionable. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Newark, N.J., Code § 2:10-11.1.
Coverage depends on owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Newark Rev. Gen. Ord. ch. 2:31, Art. 1, §§ 2:31-1 to 2:31-9.

Coverage depends on owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq..

Coverage depends on owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A0359.explanation: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not use software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information to coordinate, recommend or implement rents, lease terms or occupancy levels among competing lessors. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-2.

Landlords who raise a current tenant's rent by more than 10% year over year at lease renewal must give written disclosures before the increase takes effect: an itemization of costs behind the increase, whether a rent algorithm was used, notice of the tenant's right to sue if the increase is unconscionable or unlawful, and Division of Housing contact information. This is a disclosure rule, not a cap on the amount of the increase. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Hoboken City Code § 158-1.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Hoboken City Code ch. 155, §§ 155-3, 155-4, 155-5.

A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. The cap is adjusted each January 1 for CPI increases, starting the year after enactment. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the good causes listed in the statute, which the landlord must prove in court. A Notice to Quit (and in some cases a Notice to Cease) is required for every ground except nonpayment of rent. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

New Jersey has no statewide numeric rent cap, but a landlord may only evict for nonpayment of a rent increase if the increase is not unconscionable and complies with any municipal rent ordinance; the increase requires termination of the old lease with a Notice to Quit and notice of rent increase, and rent cannot be raised mid-lease. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone with a Section 8 HUD voucher based solely on that source of income. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq..

Housing providers may not ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record, orally or in writing, until after making a conditional offer. After that, they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, and may withdraw the offer only after an individualized assessment showing a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest. The act takes effect on the first day of the seventh month after the June 18, 2021 enactment, which works out to 2022-01-01. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64 (P.L. 2021, c.110).

A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any yearly increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid rent, including last month's rent, counts toward the cap; the deposit must be held in an interest-bearing account in trust for the tenant and returned with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2; N.J.S.A. 46:8-19; N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1; N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

New Jersey's security deposit law applies to all rental units used as homes. The only exception is owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units, and that exception ends once the tenant gives the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Hoboken, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A0360.explanation: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ban is enforced both by public authorities and through private lawsuits. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Code § 218-12.

Jersey City regulates rent increases under its Rent Control Ordinance, which the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers and enforces. Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt, and other exemptions in the ordinance may be requested. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Mun. Code ch. 260.

They may use any reasonable selection standard, such as ability to pay rent, only if it is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants. Covers this Cambridge, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cambridge Mun. Code ch. 14.04.

Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63, as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S..

An owner who charges a fee for a credit report or to process a rental application must first give the applicant a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the state maximum fee cap. This can be in the application or in a separate disclosure given before the fee is received. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.010.

Owners and their agents cannot charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees tied to a roommate leaving or to adding or replacing a roommate. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.016.

Owners must pay relocation assistance to tenants evicted for owner move-in. The payment is adjusted each year for inflation, and the Rent Board publishes the new amounts. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for rent debt below one month's HUD Fair Market Rent, bars eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease, tightens lease-breach evictions, and requires eviction notices to reference the Rent Board and be filed with it within three business days. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

Owners who evict tenants to remove a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions, adjusted yearly for inflation. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.77.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions. This includes refusing to rent, ending a tenancy, charging a higher deposit or rent, or refusing to add a family member because of criminal history. If a landlord takes action based on criminal history under an exception, the landlord must give written notice and a chance to respond. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.106.

Landlords of units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year. If the tenant moves out before the end of the year, the landlord must pay a prorated amount. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

No one may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust or conspiracy to restrain trade. No one may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. A common pricing algorithm is any method, including software, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

Landlords may charge a capped screening fee only to cover the cost of screening, such as a credit report. They must give receipts, itemized costs, a copy of any credit report and a refund of unused fees, and they must accept a reusable screening report. They cannot charge a fee when no unit is available, and they must return fees to applicants not selected unless they use a first-qualified-applicant policy. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on year built, owner occupied, owner is corporation, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26 – 2/28/27 the amount is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower income households (80% AMI or lower) displaced by demolition of their units for new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code § 7260 et seq. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6.
Coverage depends on year built, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Housing providers may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests not leading to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot have blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and time elapsed. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

Housing providers may not refuse to rent to, or set different terms for, applicants or tenants because of how they will pay rent, including Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. They must also comply with the requirements of rental assistance programs, such as completing required paperwork. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

When an applicant has a government rent subsidy, a housing provider may not use the applicant's credit history unless it offers the option to give other lawful, verifiable proof of ability to pay the tenant's share of rent. If the applicant chooses this option, the provider must give reasonable time to respond and must reasonably consider that evidence instead of credit history. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. A small landlord (a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units) may charge up to two months' rent, except to a service member. The landlord must return the remaining deposit with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant moves out. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

A landlord may evict a tenant from a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance only for one of 17 listed just cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. The end of a lease or a change in ownership is not just cause, and removing housing services such as parking, storage or laundry also requires just cause. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9.

A landlord who evicts tenants under the Ellis Act (withdrawing units from the rental market) must pay relocation money to each tenant, up to a per-unit maximum. There is an extra amount for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Amounts adjust each year based on the date the eviction notice is served. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. A landlord who evicts for owner or relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of the unit from housing use, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation money to each tenant, up to a per-unit maximum. There is an extra amount for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children. Amounts adjust each year based on the date the eviction notice is served. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code § 37.9C.

For rent-controlled units in San Francisco, the annual allowable rent increase effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6% of the tenant's base rent. The prior period (March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026) allowed 1.4%. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code ch. 37.

Landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the rate the Rent Board publishes each year. The rate is 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Covers this San Francisco, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: S.F. Admin. Code Ch. 49.

Landlords may not refuse, renew, end or restrict a tenancy, misrepresent availability, or advertise in a discriminatory way based on a person's source of income, including rental assistance and housing vouchers. Income standards must count all of a tenant's sources of income and the combined income of co-tenants and cosigners. Covers this San Diego, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: San Diego Mun. Code §§ 98.0801–98.0806.

A0366.explanation: A landlord or foreclosing owner who plans to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy, including by not renewing a lease, must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to Quit or non-renewal notice. The landlord must also send a copy of the notice to quit or non-renewal, with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City's Office of Housing Stability. This is a notice requirement only; it does not limit the reasons a landlord may end a tenancy. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Ordinance Sec. 10-11.7.

In Boston, landlords may not discriminate in renting housing based on protected characteristics, including the use of rental assistance such as Section 8, social security disability, and veterans vouchers. Refusing to accept rental assistance is housing discrimination. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Boston Fair Housing Regulations.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. H.5222, 194th General Court.
Proposed, not law. Would cover this building if enacted. Source: Mass. S.2983, 194th General Court.

Only a licensed broker or salesperson may charge prospective tenants a fee for finding housing. The broker must give the applicant written notice at the first personal meeting stating the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it depends on a lease being signed, and have the applicant sign it or record a refusal. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: 254 CMR 7.00.

A broker fee for finding a rental home may only be paid by the party (landlord or tenant) who originally hired and contracted with the licensed broker or salesperson. A landlord cannot pass the fee for a broker it hired on to the tenant. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 112, § 87DDD1/2 (as amended by St. 2025, c. 9, § 43).

At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or the landlord's agent may not require a tenant or applicant to pay the landlord or agent anything beyond first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and the cost of buying and installing a lock and key. As amended by St. 2025, c. 9, effective August 1, 2025, the limit expressly covers payments to the landlord's agent (e.g., broker fees); before that date the text applied to 'lessor' only. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B.

Either party may end a tenancy at will with written notice of three months, or, if rent is paid more often, notice equal to the rent interval or 30 days, whichever is longer. This section does not require the landlord to give a reason. For nonpayment of rent, a 14-day written notice to quit is enough, but a tenant who has not received such a notice in the prior 12 months can stop the termination by paying all rent due within 10 days. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 12.

Anyone renting housing may not discriminate against a person because they receive public assistance or a federal, state or local housing subsidy, such as rental assistance or a voucher. They also may not discriminate because of any requirement of that assistance or subsidy program. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: M.G.L. c. 151B, § 4.

A landlord may not charge a security deposit greater than the first month's rent. The deposit must be kept in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account, earn interest for the tenant, and be returned (less lawful, itemized deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Boston, MA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 186, § 15B.

This can be in the application or in a separate disclosure given before the fee is received. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.010.

Owners and their agents cannot charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy. This includes fees tied to a roommate leaving or to adding or replacing a roommate. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.016.

Owners must pay relocation assistance to tenants evicted for owner move-in. The payment is adjusted each year for inflation, and the Rent Board publishes the new amounts. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for just cause. Measure BB bars eviction for rent debt below one month's HUD Fair Market Rent, bars eviction for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease, tightens lease-breach evictions, and requires eviction notices to reference the Rent Board and be filed with it within three business days. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

Owners who evict tenants to remove a property from the rental market under the Ellis Act must pay the same relocation assistance as for owner move-in evictions, adjusted yearly for inflation. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.77.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

Rental housing providers in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions. This includes refusing to rent, ending a tenancy, charging a higher deposit or rent, or refusing to add a family member because of criminal history. If a landlord takes action based on criminal history under an exception, the landlord must give written notice and a chance to respond. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.106.

Landlords of units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year. If the tenant moves out before the end of the year, the landlord must pay a prorated amount. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76.

No one may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust or conspiracy to restrain trade. No one may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or commercial term. A common pricing algorithm is any method, including software, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729.

Landlords may charge a capped screening fee only to cover the cost of screening, such as a credit report. They must give receipts, itemized costs, a copy of any credit report and a refund of unused fees, and they must accept a reusable screening report. They cannot charge a fee when no unit is available, and they must return fees to applicants not selected unless they use a first-qualified-applicant policy. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6.
Coverage depends on year built, owner occupied, owner is corporation, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

For temporary capital improvement evictions lasting less than 20 days, relocation payments are governed by California Civil Code Section 1947.9 rather than the Rent Ordinance. For notices served 3/01/26 – 2/28/27 the amount is $446.00 per day per tenant household plus actual moving expenses. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9.

Lower income households (80% AMI or lower) displaced by demolition of their units for new construction must receive relocation benefits consistent with those public entities must pay under Government Code § 7260 et seq. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6.
Coverage depends on year built, owner is corporation, owner occupied, which the public records do not include. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12.

Housing providers may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests not leading to conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot have blanket bans on people with criminal histories. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering the nature and severity of the crime and time elapsed. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

Housing providers may not refuse to rent to, or set different terms for, applicants or tenants because of how they will pay rent, including Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers and other rental assistance. They must also comply with the requirements of rental assistance programs, such as completing required paperwork. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

When an applicant has a government rent subsidy, a housing provider may not use the applicant's credit history unless it offers the option to give other lawful, verifiable proof of ability to pay the tenant's share of rent. If the applicant chooses this option, the provider must give reasonable time to respond and must reasonably consider that evidence instead of credit history. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955.

A landlord may not demand or receive security, however named, of more than one month's rent on top of the first month's rent. A small landlord (a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units) may charge up to two months' rent, except to a service member. The landlord must return the remaining deposit with an itemized statement within 21 calendar days after the tenant moves out. Covers this Berkeley, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5.

Landlords of covered rental units in Los Angeles may not end a tenancy without one of the listed at-fault or no-fault just causes, and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. Landlords must also register units annually, give required tenant notices, and file eviction notices with LAHD. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Mun. Code § 165.00 et seq..

A landlord who demolishes a Protected Unit for new construction must pay relocation assistance at the higher of state Housing Crisis Act or City amounts, with lower income tenants receiving enhanced standardized payments ($115,480 extremely low, $96,750 very low, $87,450 low income for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027), and must provide other occupant protections. Above-low-income tenants receive the RSO/JCO amounts. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: L.A. Ordinances No. 188481 and No. 188482.

Before any no-fault eviction from a unit covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and pay relocation assistance based on the tenant's status (eligible or qualified), length of tenancy and income. For July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, amounts are $11,000 or $14,400 for eligible households and $23,150 or $27,400 for qualified households, with reduced amounts for Mom and Pop owner-occupancy evictions ($10,550 / $21,250) and one month's rent for JCO single-family homes owned by natural persons. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: LAMC 151.09, 151.30, 165.03, 165.06.

For RSO units, rent may be increased only once every 12 months, by the allowable rent increase percentage set by LAHD. As of February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer add an extra percentage for utilities, and rent can reset to market rate only after certain vacancies or evictions. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Chapter XV, Article 1.

The RSO covers interest payments on security deposits for RSO units. This page does not state the rate or timing. Covers this Los Angeles, CA building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Los Angeles Municipal Code Chapter XV, Article 1.

A0371.explanation: Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: Newark, N.J., Code § 19:2-3.1; § 19:2-3.2.

Defines an unconscionable rent as a residential rent increase that is exceedingly harsh or unreasonable, exceeds the increase in the landlord's expenses, and is not comparable to rents at similar properties. For properties under a redevelopment or financial agreement, rent above the approved pro-forma is per se unconscionable. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Newark, N.J., Code § 2:10-11.1.

Landlords and real estate brokers may ask about or consider an applicant's criminal history only after a formal application is submitted, with prior written notice and consent. They may look only at indictable convictions within 8 years and disorderly persons convictions within 5 years of release or sentencing, plus pending charges and certain serious offenses at any time. They may not consider arrests without conviction, expunged or sealed records, or juvenile adjudications, and must weigh rehabilitation, time passed, and the nature of the offense. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Newark Rev. Gen. Ord. ch. 2:31, Art. 1, §§ 2:31-1 to 2:31-9.

A landlord or agent may not require an application or similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property that exceeds $50. The cap is adjusted each January 1 for CPI increases, starting the year after enactment. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-18.1 (P.L. 2025, c.405).

A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a written or oral lease without one of the good causes listed in the statute, which the landlord must prove in court. A Notice to Quit (and in some cases a Notice to Cease) is required for every ground except nonpayment of rent. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.

New Jersey has no statewide numeric rent cap, but a landlord may only evict for nonpayment of a rent increase if the increase is not unconscionable and complies with any municipal rent ordinance; the increase requires termination of the old lease with a Notice to Quit and notice of rent increase, and rent cannot be raised mid-lease. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1.
Coverage depends on year built, which the public records do not include. Source: N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5.

Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone with a Section 8 HUD voucher based solely on that source of income. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 10:5-1 et seq..

Housing providers may not ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record, orally or in writing, until after making a conditional offer. After that, they may consider only certain convictions within set lookback periods, and may withdraw the offer only after an individualized assessment showing a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest. The act takes effect on the first day of the seventh month after the June 18, 2021 enactment, which works out to 2022-01-01. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64 (P.L. 2021, c.110).

A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any yearly increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid rent, including last month's rent, counts toward the cap; the deposit must be held in an interest-bearing account in trust for the tenant and returned with interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2; N.J.S.A. 46:8-19; N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1; N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

New Jersey's security deposit law applies to all rental units used as homes. The only exception is owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units, and that exception ends once the tenant gives the landlord 30 days' written notice invoking the act. Covers this Newark, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: N.J.S.A. 46:8-26.

A0372.explanation: Landlords may not use algorithmic rent coordination services. The ban is enforced both by public authorities and through private lawsuits. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Code § 218-12.

Jersey City regulates rent increases under its Rent Control Ordinance, which the Office of Landlord/Tenant Relations administers and enforces. Properties with 1 to 4 units are exempt, and other exemptions in the ordinance may be requested. Covers this Jersey City, NJ building as of 2026-10-01. Source: Jersey City Mun. Code ch. 260.
